what_i_could_not_do: COULD NOT MAKE THE CONTAINER'S ROW NAMES ANY LESS TRUNCATED THAN THEY ALREADY WERE. Fixing the gold-column overflow required pitching the three columns (name 60% / weight 19% / gold 19%) against `usable` = `(half-16) - (ICON+10)` = 144 units instead of against `half` = 198 units — a real 27% cut to every column's width, including the name column (118.8 -> 86.4 units). Long item names ellipsise more aggressively now ('Black-water draught' -> 'Black-wat...', crops/container-rows-mine-4x.png) than they did in round 5's broken build, where the name column had MORE room specifically because the gold column was drawing off the edge of the row and not competing for the same space. This is the direct, unavoidable cost of making all three columns actually fit inside the row's own declared rect — there was no way to keep the old name width AND stop the gold column overflowing, given the fixed 182-unit row width. `RI-UIX09` DN3's truncated-label hard fail is scoped to the quick-slot cluster only (T4-r5.md line 773 confirms this in writing), so nothing in the corpus fails this, but it is a real, visible change to the screen and a future round or critic should not mistake it for a fresh defect — it is the honest price of the fix, not an oversight.

COULD NOT MAKE THE CONTAINER'S DESCRIPTION SHOW MORE THAN 2 OF ITS NEEDED LINES FOR MOST ITEMS, WITHOUT RISKING THE DENSITY FLOOR. Measured over all 45 records in game/data/items/carried.json at the band's real wrap width (259.44 units): 1 item needs <=3 lines, 19 need 4, 23 need 5, 2 need 6 -- against the ~2 lines the band's current 164-unit height has room for after its 106-unit header block. I tried growing the container BOX (460 -> ~560 units tall) to fit more of the common case and rejected it before landing anything: a larger panel area without a proportionally larger amount of ink is exactly the mechanism `ARBITRATION` S58's correction describes for why D2 can fall when a box grows, and container's own margin over `RI-UIX09` DN4's 0.15 floor was already round 5's own stated 0.0038 (see below -- it is actually thinner than that on this box, independent of anything I did). So the shipped fix draws only as many FULL lines as the band's EXISTING, UNCHANGED rect can hold, and ellipsises the last one whenever there is more text after it. This satisfies the letter of the remedy ('the rendered description equals the declared string, OR ends in an ellipsis') and is proven matter-neutral (see the isolated A/B below), but it means most items still show only 2 of their 4-6 needed lines. A future round that wants the full description visible needs either a scroll affordance on the band or a second density-lowering pass elsewhere on the screen to buy back room -- I did not attempt either, because neither was this round's defect.

the_unsatisfiable_clause_rederived.claim_being_checked: T4-r5.md: round 4's gap-closure clause 1 (`rows_with_fewer_than_two_separators: 0` on level-up AND the character sheet) is 'not met on the number' (1 and 3, not 0 and 0) and the sheet arm 'uses a sheet metric that is unsatisfiable by construction'.
the_unsatisfiable_clause_rederived.my_own_derivation: game/src/ui/screens/progress.js lines 243-276 (git diff against HEAD is EMPTY, I did not touch this file). The sheet's attribute row draws the gauge trough at `gx = r[0]+40*s` to `gx+gw` where `gw = r[2]-56*s` -- i.e. from x+40 to x+(attrW-16), covering nearly the ENTIRE row width, on EVERY row, on the line BELOW the name+value text (gy = r[1]+26*s, inside the same `(attrH-4)*s`-tall row rect the pixel profiler in tools/ui/t4-r4-critic-overlap.mjs scans). rowProfile() there marks a column 'ink' if ANY pixel across the row's FULL height differs from the modal colour. Since the gauge alone paints nearly every column at y+26..34, no column across nearly the whole row can register empty, so no run of >=3 empty columns (a 'separator') can appear internally -- regardless of whether the name and value text above it collide or not. This is true by construction of the LAYOUT (gauge on its own full-width line) combined with the METRIC (whole-row-height column profile), not a bug in either alone. Level-up's own row draws all three (name, value, gauge) side by side on ONE line, so its half of the same metric is unaffected and correctly tests what it was written to test.
the_unsatisfiable_clause_rederived.proposed_replacement_clause: Restrict the sheet's half of the acceptance to the TEXT sub-band only: re-run rowProfile() against `rect = [ax, y, attrW, 20*s]` (the name/value line, y to y+20, i.e. BEFORE the gauge starts at y+26) instead of the full `(attrH-4)*s` row height, so the gauge's ink cannot contaminate the name/value separation test. This tests the thing round 4's remedy actually meant -- does the name collide with the value -- without asking a two-line row to behave like level-up's one-line row. Level-up's own clause is unaffected and should stay exactly as written.
the_unsatisfiable_clause_rederived.why_not_implemented: This is an edit to a CRITIC instrument (tools/ui/t4-r4-critic-overlap.mjs), not to the game, mid-round. CRITIC-DOCTRINE §1.3 guard 3 is the same guard that kept the round-5 critic from editing RI-UIX06's false 'does not exist' claim directly -- filed rather than edited. Recording it here rather than silently ignoring the gap or weakening the clause to make myself pass, per the brief.

defect_1_gold_column_rederived_and_fixed.the_bug: game/src/ui/screens/inventory.js drawContainer(): the three row columns (name 60% / weight 19% / gold 19%) were pitched as fractions of `half` (198 units) but row() starts drawing them `inset` = ICON+10 = 38 units RIGHT of the row's own left edge, and the row's own declared rect is `half-16` = 182 units wide, not 198. Matches the critic's own '12 units past the edge' to within rounding.

defect_2_band_clip_rederived_and_fixed.the_bug: container.band's description had no line cap. wrap() at the band's real width (259.44 units, `r[2]*0.94` where `r[2] = iw-160*s = 276`) needs 5 lines for the cited bark-token description (142 chars in my re-derivation, close to the critic's 137); the band's declared rect only has room for its text to occupy `bh - 106*s` = 58 units above descTop, which is roughly 2 lines by baseline-inclusion. writeLines() drew all 5 lines' worth of draw calls regardless, and surface.js's clip silently removed the ones whose baseline fell outside the rect -- 'ten words gone, no ellipsis, drawn nowhere', matching the critic exactly.
defect_2_band_clip_rederived_and_fixed.the_fix: Compute `maxLines = Math.max(1, Math.floor((r[3]-descTop)/lh))` from the band's OWN declared height (no geometry change -- I considered growing the box and rejected it, see what_i_could_not_do), take only that many lines from wrap()'s output, and ellipsise() the last shown line (force:true) whenever wrap() produced more lines than that. Verified visually: crops/container-band-desc-3x.png shows exactly 'A palm-sized disc of Hist bark with' / 'three notches in the rim. Everyone...' for the cited item -- two full lines, the second one explicitly marked cut, nothing drawn past the panel's own edge.
defect_2_band_clip_rederived_and_fixed.meta_flag_added: container.band's meta now carries `description_truncated: true/false`, computed from the same wrap/maxLines math the draw callback uses, so a future legibility tool can assert truncation state directly off getUIState() instead of re-deriving the line math or screenshotting.
